about: The Catchment Health scorecard (Scorecards tab): which datasets feed each measure, and how each measure is rated. Every source listed under a measure is pooled for each waterbody.
howToAddASource: Find the measure below, and add an entry to its sources list.
dataset: the dataset's id in data/catalog.json, where the app finds its service, units and how to read ranges and limits.
name: the dataset's name, as shown on the scorecard, the map and the PDF.
fields: the field or fields holding the measure, as named in the dataset.
values: absolute, range or mixed. See valueTypes.
The built-in sources (national_river_survey, riverfly and nbs_interventions) are read by the scorecard's own code, not through data/catalog.json.
howRatingsWork: Every measure is rated High, Good, Moderate, Poor or Bad.
better: higher means more is better, so a value at or above the high figure is High, at or above good is Good, and so on. Below poor is Bad.
better: lower means less is better, so a value at or below the high figure is High, at or below good is Good, and so on. Above poor is Bad.
A figure can be written as a fraction, such as "1/20".

thresholds: catalog means the measure uses its determinand's bands in data/catalog.json, the same ones that colour the Monitoring explorer, so the two can't disagree. Low is High, Slightly Elevated is Good, Elevated is Moderate, High is Poor and Very High is Bad.
statistic: mean or median, how a waterbody's readings are combined before rating.
whenNone: what a count of none means for a measure that counts things (only Action uses it so far). "no data" leaves it unrated, shown grey; "bad" rates it Bad.
A theme's rating is the average of its measures' ratings, and the overall rating the average of the themes'.

Wildlife's score is the share of surveys recording at least one indicator species, times how evenly the sightings spread across the species (the effective number of species, worked out from each species' share of the sightings, divided by the number of species). 20% of surveys with an indicator, all of them fish, scores 20% x 1/7 = 2.9%; the same 20% spread evenly across all seven species scores 20%. Its thresholds were set from the 2026 River Guardians data.
Visible Pollution's thresholds were set from the 2026 data: across the 54 southern waterbodies with enough surveys, the median share with a visible sign was 17%.
These thresholds are a provisional first pass from the National River Survey dashboard, not a reviewed standard.

valueTypes.absolute: Every value is an exact reading, such as 0.34.
valueTypes.range: Every value is a range or a step on a colour chart, such as 2-5. Each counts at the bottom of its range, so 2-5 counts as 2.
valueTypes.mixed: Mostly exact readings, with some at a limit of detection, such as 0 meaning below 0.04. Below the limit counts as 0; beyond it counts at the limit.
valueTypes.flags: One Yes/No field per sign or species, recorded as 1 or 0 (or Yes) on every survey. A survey shows it when the field is 1 or Yes. List each field and the name to show for it under signs. answeredFields, if given, are the fields of which at least one is ticked when the question was answered; other surveys are left out.
valueTypes.keywords: A free-text answer that can name several things. A survey shows a sign when its answer contains any listed keyword, ignoring capitals, spaces and underscores, so "Oily sheen" also finds "Oily_sheen". A blank answer isn't counted as a survey.

coverage.about: A waterbody needs at least this much data in the period before its nutrient, wildlife, invasives and visible pollution measures are rated. Nutrients count sites and readings, and wildlife and visible pollution sites and surveys, across all their sources; invasives counts National River Survey sites and surveys.

rating.measure: share of surveys with any visible sign of pollution
wildlife score: share of surveys with an indicator species, times how evenly sightings spread across the species

sources.name: River Guardians
sources.answeredNote: A survey counts only if it answered the wildlife question: None, or any animal ticked. Ducks, moorhens, coots, geese, swans and Other show it was answered but aren't indicator species.
